bibliography.title: To Grok Grokking: Provable Grokking in Ridge Regression
bibliography.version_read: arXiv:2601.19791v4, dated 2026-07-16 on the PDF title page

sections.title: 4.1. Warmup: Grokking with the Zero Teacher
6. Discussion: explicit open questions and scope

abstract_sentences.text: We study grokking—the onset of generalization long after overfitting—in a classical ridge regression setting.
We prove end-to-end grokking results for learning over-parameterized linear regression models using gradient descent with weight decay.

Specifically, we prove that the following stages occur: (i) the model overfits the training data early during training; (ii) poor generalization persists long after overfitting has manifested; and (iii) the generalization error eventually becomes arbitrarily small.
Moreover, we show, both theoretically and empirically, that grokking can be amplified or eliminated in a principled manner through proper hyperparameter tuning.
To the best of our knowledge, these are the first rigorous quantitative bounds on the generalization delay (which we refer to as the “grokking time”) in terms of training hyperparameters.
Lastly, going beyond the linear setting, we empirically demonstrate that our quantitative bounds also capture the behavior of grokking on non-linear neural networks.

Our results suggest that grokking is not an inherent failure mode of deep learning, but rather a consequence of specific training conditions, and thus does not require fundamental changes to the model architecture or learning algorithm to avoid.

experimental_design.name: theoretical teacher-student problem
experimental_design.description: Inputs follow an unspecified Dx, labels are exact teacher outputs, the feature map is fixed, and the teacher is realizable by theta*. The trainable student is linear in that map.

experimental_design.name: grokking success criterion
experimental_design.description: t1 is the last time empirical loss is at least epsilon and t2 is the first time population loss is at most c, with c at least epsilon.

experimental_design.name: Figure 1 replication unit
experimental_design.description: The caption identifies 50 independent runs with independent datasets and student initializations; it compares train and test squared losses on a log training-step axis.

experimental_design.name: Figure 2 realizable-ridge setup
experimental_design.description: Uses identity features, a unit-norm realizable teacher, Gaussian feature specialization, eta=1, and default n=100, m=1000, nu^2=1, lambda=10^-4; c=epsilon=0.01.

experimental_design.name: Figure 3 random-features setup
experimental_design.description: A two-layer random ReLU feature student trains only its output layer against an independently sampled single-ReLU teacher; d=100 and the stated defaults are n=100, lambda=10^-5, m=10000, nu^2=1.

experimental_design.name: Figure 4 full-ReLU setup
experimental_design.description: Both layers train against a zero teacher with d=50, eta=10^-4, and defaults n=50, m=1000, nu^2=1, lambda=0.05.

experimental_design.name: implementation and compute disclosure
experimental_design.description: The PDF does not identify code source, hardware, seed values, total training budget, test-set size, or a run count for Figures 2–4.

limitations.name: realizability and fixed-feature scope
limitations.description: The central theorem assumes a realizable teacher, fixed feature map, bounded features, overparameterization, and a small weight-decay regime.

limitations.name: non-realizable ridge regression
limitations.description: Section 6 names non-realizable ridge regression, including label noise, as an open end-to-end theorem question.

limitations.name: nonlinear theorem gap
limitations.description: The paper says current analysis does not identify a nonlinear hyperparameter realization and that NTK closeness does not prove persistent poor generalization.

limitations.name: small-lambda agnostic failure mode
limitations.description: For agnostic learning, arbitrarily small weight decay may impede generalization entirely under the authors techniques.

limitations.name: empirical uncertainty disclosure

final_judgment.single_storyline: In overparameterized ridge GD, fast fitting in the data row space and slow weight-decay shrinkage in its orthogonal complement separate t1 from t2; eventual regularization enables generalization.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body keeps the model, objective, GD rule, t1/t2 definitions, main theorem statements, mechanism, sufficient conditions, and Figures 1–4.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: The appendix carries proof details, the Gaussian specialization of Equation (8), threshold/noise/RFF experiments, and the chi-squared lemma; theorem validity therefore needs Appendix A for full verification.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Theorems 4.4, 4.5, and 4.6 separately certify fast training fit, persistent poor generalization, and eventual generalization, while Figure 2 uses the same t1/t2 variables to test the predicted hyperparameter directions.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The strongest reader cost is the gap from a tightly conditional linear theorem to qualitative nonlinear curves with sparse replication and uncertainty disclosure.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For delayed-generalization work, define two observable time points, give a separate evidentiary route for each, and reuse the same mechanism variables in equations, figure axes, and conclusion.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule needs stable training and generalization time scales. It should not be imposed where the metric or learning dynamics makes such times undefined or unstable.
